questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: academic opportunities

Additional comments:
questions.answer: Really good both academic and socially

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Easy but also a bit strange since it was covid and everything was online

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received keys to housing ect. and emails with course instructions

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: There were no such welcome unfortunately

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: SSSB site if you can't get a place through university housing

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Lappis is so beautiful, near forest and water. If you want social stuff too i really recommend this place.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Easy but weird to be left a bit alone with it all because it was online

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I was just registered from the beginning i think, and that part was easy

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Only email contact

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be aware that there is both an english and swedish course page. I registered for some swedish courses too that wasn't shown in the english page. I could submit my exam in danish.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Much more practical work, and smaller but more frequently assignments. This i loved! Was able to take writing courses, this was amazing!

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had courses for both BA and MA

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Much more practical work, and smaller but more frequently assignments. Easier to overcome for me, but also more structure in this sense.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 2 semesters

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Creative writing and reading
Swedish literature
Creative writing in English

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
questions.answer:
Love, Resistance, Media. The practices of writing and reading. 
Journalistic Writing.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you like writing I highly recommend these courses. Some was online, so maybe not the best option if you aim for socializing (was during covid anyway for me).

Additional comments:
questions.answer: There are plenty of oportunities I think, but I was away during covid

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is a thursday bar/club Böjan and sports activities i think

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Walk or run in the woods, swim in the lakes when summer (or winter), go to botanical garden and cafe, fika, libraries, Yoga in Södermalm. You can sign in to Sats from denmark and don't pay that much extra to train in Sweden. If you want fitness and don't have a personnumber this is a good option. The one in Vasastan (In Radisson)b has a pool!!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to concerts, walk or run in the woods, swim in the lakes when summer (or winter), go to botanical garden and cafe, fika, libraries, Yoga in Södermalm. Hiking in Nacka or other places in the Arcipelago, in general visit the islands around Stockholm.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Swedish are a bit closed and hard to become friends with, but be persistent. When they open up they are the sweetest.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: more closed than danes, super polite but hard to figure out.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Fika!! And the closeness to nature. A calm attitude too

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Use the university outdoor and indoor facilities. You end up loving that place. Don't be scared of getting international friends. People in Stockholm can be challenging to get to know. I recommend  living in the student areas like Lappis. I was skeptical about this myself (I'm a bit older and don't likle the usual, sometimes forced student socialization, but i really don't regret it).

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Get a person number if you can, makes everything easier. Biking is not a easy in Stockholm as you thing. I recommend a really good bike to all the hills.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The academic courses where I got to write and all the friends I met and people from all kind of cultures.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Covid

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Stockholm is so great! I dosen't seem far away, but you will notice all the small differences.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
